literal: Xing Shao, styled Zicai, a man of Mo in Hejian, descendant of Wei Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhen.
idiomatic: Biography of Xing Shao. Xing Shao, styled Zicai, was from Mo in Hejian commandery; he descended from Grand Master of Ceremonies Zhen of Wei.

literal: His father Qiu was Wei Director of the Imperial Household.
idiomatic: His father Xing Qiu had served Wei as director of the imperial household.

literal: Shao's childhood name was Ji; in youth there was a taboo, and so he did not use his formal name.
idiomatic: Shao's childhood name was Ji; while young he observed a naming taboo and did not use his formal name.

literal: At age five, Cui Liang of Qinghe, Lang of the Ministry of Personnel in Wei, saw him and was struck, saying: "This boy will in time achieve great things; rank and repute will be universally manifest.
idiomatic: At five, Cui Liang of Qinghe, a lang in the Wei ministry of personnel, saw him and marveled, saying, "This child will one day achieve great things; office and fame will spread far and wide.

literal: " At ten he could compose in writing; elegant in talent and thought, clever and with a strong memory, he recited more than ten thousand words a day.
idiomatic: " By ten he could write compositions; gifted and inventive, sharp-witted and retentive, he recited more than ten thousand words each day.

literal: His clansman Luan, who had judgment of human character, told the younger kin: "In our lineage there is this boy—a man not of the common sort.
idiomatic: His kinsman Luan, skilled at judging men, told the younger generation, "Our house has produced this boy—he is no ordinary person.

literal: " In youth he was in Luoyang; the realm was at peace, and with the day's eminent men he devoted himself solely to touring mountains and waters and feasting for pleasure, with no leisure for diligent study.
idiomatic: " While young in Luoyang, the empire was quiet; with celebrated contemporaries he gave himself only to landscape outings and banquets, leaving no time for steady application.

literal: Once during prolonged rain he read the History of Han; in five days he could largely remember it through.
idiomatic: Once, during long rains, he took up the History of Han and within five days could recall most of it.

literal: Later, wearied of drinking and jesting, he broadly sought out the classics and histories; with five lines at once under his eye, one reading and he remembered—nothing was lost.
idiomatic: Later, tired of drink and banter, he turned widely to the classics and histories; reading five lines at a glance, he retained each passage at once.

literal: His compositions were classical and beautiful, ample yet swift.
idiomatic: His writing was elegant and polished, copious yet quick.

literal: Before he was twenty his name stirred the gentry.
idiomatic: Before twenty his reputation had shaken the official class.

literal: He once lodged and drank overnight at the house of the Prince of Beihai, Xin, with Youbei Pingyang Gu, Hedong Pei Bomo, his cousin from the father's line Fei, and Henan Lu Daohui; together they composed poems, several dozen in all, and all were left with the host's servant.
idiomatic: Once he stayed overnight drinking at Prince Xin of Beihai's residence with Pingyang Gu of Youbei, Pei Bomo of Hedong, his paternal cousin Fei, and Lu Daohui of Henan; they composed several dozen poems together, all left with the host's servant.

literal: Next morning the servant went out; the others could not recover their poems, but Shao recited every one from memory.
idiomatic: At dawn the servant went abroad; the others could not find their poems, but Shao recited them all.

literal: Some among them did not recognize their own poems; when the servant returned with the originals, not a single character was wrong.
idiomatic: Some did not recognize their own work; when the servant brought back the originals, not one character differed.

literal: The company thereupon ranked him with Wang Can.
idiomatic: The company then compared him to Wang Can.

literal: Li Shenjun of Longxi, Minister of Personnel, greatly esteemed him and made him a friend across the years.
idiomatic: Li Shenjun of Longxi, minister of personnel, held him in high regard and took him as a friend despite the age gap.

literal: He doffed mourning and became a Wei mourning officer for Emperor Xuanwu, was appointed gentleman attendant at court, and was promoted assistant in the Bureau of Weights and Measures.
idiomatic: Leaving mourning, he served as a Wei mourning officer for Emperor Xuanwu, was made gentleman attendant at court, and rose to assistant in the bureau of weights and measures.

literal: He was deeply honored by the commander of the guards Yuan Cha; when Cha had just been appointed Director of the Masters of Writing, Shenjun and Yuan Fan of Chen commandery were at the feast, and Cha had Shao draft a letter of thanks—in a moment it was done, and shown to the guests.
idiomatic: The commander of the guards Yuan Cha treated him with great respect; when Cha had just become director of the masters of writing, Shenjun and Yuan Fan of Chen were present, and Cha had Shao write a letter of thanks—it was finished at once and shown round.

literal: Shenjun said: "This memorial of Xing Shao's is enough to make Master Yuan change color.
idiomatic: Shenjun said, "This table from Xing Shao alone would make Master Yuan flush.

literal: " At the beginning of Xiaochang he and Yellow Gate Attendant Li Yanzhi jointly oversaw court ritual.
idiomatic: " At the opening of Xiaochang he and yellow gate attendant Li Yanzhi jointly directed court ceremonial.

literal: After Emperor Xiaoming, letters flourished greatly; Shao's ornamental beauty in writing stood alone in his age—whenever a piece first appeared, the capital ran short of paper for it, and within moments it was read and chanted near and far.
idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaoming of Wei, literary culture flourished; Shao's ornamental prose stood alone—each new piece made paper dear in the capital, and within moments it was read and recited across the realm.

literal: At the time Yuan Fan and Zu Ying of Fanyang, lofty in rank and repute, were praised by elders for the beauty of their brush; seeing Shao's florid, brilliant thought, they deeply envied him together.
idiomatic: Yuan Fan and Zu Ying of Fanyang were then eminent in office and fame, their writing praised by seniors; Shao's lush brilliance they jointly resented.

literal: Whenever a noble in Luoyang took a new post, he mostly relied on Shao for the letter of thanks.
idiomatic: Whenever a Luoyang grandee assumed a new post, he usually had Shao draft the letter of thanks.

literal: Once a powerful man had just received office and gave a great feast for guests; Fan and Shao were both seated.
idiomatic: Once a powerful man had just received appointment and held a great banquet; Fan and Shao were both present.

literal: Fan supposed the host had entrusted him with the declination memorial and thereupon ordered Shao to write it.
idiomatic: Fan assumed the host meant him to write the declination and ordered Shao to do it instead.

literal: Fan was very displeased and often told others: "The Xing boy should, when a guest, compose his own memorials—buy his own yellow paper, write it, and send it in.
idiomatic: Fan was deeply displeased and often said, "That Xing boy ought to write his own memorials as a guest—buy his own yellow paper, draft it, and submit it himself.

literal: " Shao feared harm from Fan and pleaded illness.
idiomatic: " Shao feared Fan would injure him and pleaded illness.

literal: When Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo went out to command Qing province, he recommended Shao as staff secretary of the headquarters.
idiomatic: When director of the masters of writing Yuan Luo took command of Qing province, he had Shao appointed headquarters staff secretary.

literal: He remained in the eastern lands, drinking and enjoying himself all day, exhausting the charm of mountains and springs.
idiomatic: He stayed in the east, feasting and savoring all day, draining every delight of hill and stream.

literal: At the beginning of Yong'an he was promoted repeatedly to Secretariat Attendant; the edicts and pronouncements he drafted were grand and beautiful in style.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yong'an he rose repeatedly to secretariat attendant; his edicts and pronouncements were magnificent in diction.

literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang the capital was in turmoil; Shao and Yang Yin of Hongnong took refuge on Mount Song.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and the capital fell into chaos, Shao and Yang Yin of Hongnong fled to Mount Song.

literal: In Putai he was concurrently Attendant of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat; soon after he became Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
idiomatic: In Putai he was made concurrent attendant of the yellow gate in the secretariat, then regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was ordered to remain constantly on duty in the inner court, given imperial meals, and charged to review affairs of the Masters of Writing and the Secretariat; for every great appointment he was first asked whether it was permissible, and only then was it carried out.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was ordered to keep constant watch in the inner court, supplied with imperial food, and told to review business of the masters of writing and secretariat; major appointments were first referred to him for approval.

literal: He was appointed General of the Guards and Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: He was made general of the guards and grand master of the imperial academy.

literal: Because his parents were aged he returned home; an edict ordered the locality to grant him especially five soldiers of force, and also to enter court once a year as adviser.
idiomatic: When his parents grew old he went home; the throne ordered his district to assign him five guards and to let him attend court once a year for consultation.

literal: On completing mourning for his mother his grief exceeded the rites.
idiomatic: Mourning his mother, he grieved beyond what the rites prescribed.

literal: Later Yang Yin with Wei Shou and Shao requested the establishment of schools and the repair and erection of the Bright Hall, memorializing:
idiomatic: Later Yang Yin, Wei Shou, and Shao petitioned to establish schools and rebuild the Bright Hall, writing:

literal: The Ancestral Chamber and Bright Hall were illustrious in Zhou and Xia;
idiomatic: The Ancestral Chamber and Bright Hall shone forth under Zhou and Xia;

literal: one academy and two schools flourished from the time of Yu and Yin.
idiomatic: a single academy and paired schools flourished from Yu and Yin.

literal: Thereby to sacrifice to the Lord on High and display the utmost majesty;
idiomatic: By them the realm sacrificed to the Lord on High and showed the greatest solemnity;

literal: to proclaim across the lower realm and manifest the pattern of matching Heaven.
idiomatic: they proclaimed to the four quarters and embodied Heaven's model of rule.

literal: To nourish white-haired elders in seeking wise words, to rear blue-collared youths in spreading the teaching canon—thereby states enjoyed long endurance and their emblems through ten thousand sacrifices.
idiomatic: They nourished gray hair to seek wisdom and reared blue collars to spread the teaching canon—thus realms endured and their fame lasted ten thousand generations.

literal: When it reached the fallen Qin, it reformed their Way, buried the ru and extinguished learning, to blind the black-haired people.
idiomatic: Then Qin fell, altered the Way, buried scholars and ended learning, and darkened the common folk.

literal: Hence the nine domains split apart and the mandate ended after two generations.
idiomatic: The nine domains shattered and the throne passed after only two generations.

literal: The blazing Han rose vigorously and again repaired ru learning.
idiomatic: Han rose in flame and again restored Confucian learning.

literal: Hence in the Western Capital were the meaning of six schools; in the Eastern Capital the splendor of three academies.
idiomatic: In the western capital stood the six schools; in the eastern capital the glory of three academies.

literal: Down through Wei and Jin, in turmoil one after another, amid arms and armor the schools did not perish.
idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward, rebellion followed rebellion, yet amid war the schools never ceased.

literal: Looking up, Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, the High Ancestor, received the sage from Heaven; his Way mirrors present and past; he arrayed schools in the districts and thickly spread the Odes and Documents through the commanderies.
idiomatic: We look up to Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, the High Ancestor, who received the sage from Heaven and whose Way reflects all ages—he ordered schools in the hamlets and spread the Odes and Documents through every commandery.

literal: But the founding enterprise was pressing, the martial chariot was repeatedly driven forth; there was no leisure to accomplish much—the bow and sword could not be followed up.
idiomatic: Yet the founding work pressed hard and the war chariot rode out again and again; he had no leisure to finish—bow and sword were left behind.

literal: Emperor Wuzong of Wei continued the former thread; in Yongping he greatly raised timber and earthworks.
idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong of Wei took up the former thread; in Yongping he launched great construction.

literal: Then came flood and drought, war-horses at the suburbs; though the mountain was nearly heaped, one basket of earth still halted.
idiomatic: Then flood and drought came, war-horses at the suburbs; though the mound was nearly made, one basket of earth remained undone.

literal: Yet the root of Bright Hall, rites and music, became a thicket of brambles and thorns;
idiomatic: The root of rites and music, the Bright Hall, became a tangle of thorns;

literal: the foundation of virtue and righteousness in the school halls stood empty, filled only with the tracks of herd-boys;
idiomatic: the school halls, foundation of virtue and duty, stood empty but for herd-boys' footprints;

literal: the weight of stern ramparts and walls lacked the work of brick and stone;
idiomatic: the ramparts, weight of defense, lacked brick and stone;

literal: the essentials of lofty terraces and structures had little adornment of towers and pavilions.
idiomatic: the lofty terraces that display imperial majesty had scarcely tower or pavilion.

literal: Added to this, wind and rain gradually encroached, and bit by bit they fell into ruin.
idiomatic: Wind and rain wore at them until they crumbled.

literal: This is not what is called pursuing the loftiness of the hall's frame and taking the rites as model for ten thousand states.
idiomatic: This is not to pursue a lofty hall nor to make ritual the model for ten thousand states.

literal: We have heard that court discussion, because the High Ancestor greatly fashioned the realm within the four seas and his Way matched King Wen of Zhou, raised the record of the Bright Hall to match the Lord on High.
idiomatic: We hear the court argues that because the High Ancestor shaped the realm within the four seas and his Way matched King Wen of Zhou, he raised the Bright Hall to sacrifice to the Lord on High.

literal: If now the foundation is not repaired, it is the same as a hillock in a field; even if the High Emperor's spirit is offered to, it is lacking at the national yang; the canon of ancestral service has sound without substance.
idiomatic: If the foundations are not restored, it is but a mound in a field—even the High Emperor's spirit lacks its seat in the national altar; ancestral rite has sound without substance.

literal: This is why ministers and sons are uneasy and the hundred millions stand waiting.
idiomatic: Hence ministers cannot rest and the people wait in hope.

literal: Your subject has also heard that the official realm grants ability so as to charge with affairs; once charged, salary rewards the service.
idiomatic: We also hear that office grants ability to bear tasks, and tasks once borne are repaid with salary.

literal: Thus above there is no censure of vacant posts; below there is no slander of those who eat salary and do nothing.
idiomatic: Then above none blame vacant posts; below none mock salary without work.

literal: Now the Imperial Academy, though it has the name of a school office, has no reality of instruction—how is it different from dodder on wheat, or the Winnow Basket and Northern Dipper?
idiomatic: Today the imperial academy bears the name of a teaching office yet has no teaching—no different from dodder on wheat, or the Winnow Basket and Northern Dipper stars.

literal: Formerly Liu Xiang said that a king should raise the Bright Academy and display rites and music to transform the realm.
idiomatic: Liu Xiang once said a king should raise the Bright Academy and display rites and music to sway the realm.

literal: Rites and music are for nourishing men; penal law is for killing men—yet the offices are diligent in requesting the fixing of penal law, while of rites and music they say they dare not yet.
idiomatic: Rites and music nourish men; penal law kills them—yet officials press eagerly to fix penal law, while of rites and music they say they dare not.

literal: This is daring to kill men and not daring to nourish men.
idiomatic: They dare kill but dare not nourish.

literal: Your subject considers that now within the four seas all is clear and level, the nine domains tranquil and feasting; the essentials of governing the state ought first to be honored—if again delayed, Liu Xiang's words will prove true.
idiomatic: We hold that with the four seas calm and the nine domains at peace, the state's first duty should be honored—delay again, and Liu Xiang's warning will come true.

literal: But two things cannot be raised at once; advance and retreat must be chosen.
idiomatic: Yet two great works cannot rise together; there must be choice between advance and retreat.

literal: By your subject's dull reckoning, one should stop the ornate works of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories, considerably reduce the timber-and-earth projects of Yongning, likewise cut the tile-and-timber of Yaoguang, share out the labor of carving the stone grottoes, and all other tasks not urgent to the age; in the three seasons' gaps in farming, repair these several items.
idiomatic: In our humble judgment, stop the directorate's ornamental works, cut Yongning's timber and earth, reduce Yaoguang's tile and timber, divide the labor of the stone grottoes, and every task not urgent to the age; in the three seasons' farming gaps, repair these several works.

literal: Then the rites of the Bright Academy will luxuriantly revive;
idiomatic: Then Bright Hall ritual will flourish again;

literal: the sound of chanting and recitation will blaze forth anew; fine terraces and high walls will be stern and strong without, the locust palace and thorn offices bright and splendid within.
idiomatic: chanting and recitation will blaze anew; fine towers and high walls will stand stern without, the academy and law courts bright within.

literal: Further clarify past and present, again honor district drinking, urge forward commandery schools, examine closely classic studies—thus Yuan and Kai may be obtained in the upper sequence, You and Xia brought forth in the lower states; would it not be glorious!
idiomatic: Clarify past and present, restore district drinking, advance commandery schools, test classic learning—then Yuan and Kai may appear in the capital schools, You and Xia in the provinces; would that not be glorious!

literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered: "The great rite of matching sacrifice is the root of the state; because war-horses were at the suburbs, repair could not be hurried.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered, "The great rite of matching sacrifice is the root of the state; war-horses at the suburbs left no leisure for repair.

literal: Now the four quarters are tranquil and secure; the relevant offices should be ordered separately to deliberate on the founding enterprise."
idiomatic: Now the four quarters are calm; let the proper offices separately plan the founding work."

literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Grand Master of Ceremonies and Secretariat Supervisor, acting Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to grand master of ceremonies and secretariat supervisor, acting grand master of the imperial academy.

literal: At the time many court ministers held a single office; few concurrently led two posts—Shao suddenly held three, all at the head of letters, and the age honored him.
idiomatic: Most ministers then held one post; few bore two—Shao at once held three, each at the summit of literary office, and his contemporaries envied him.

literal: Gao Yang visited Jinyang; on the road sweet dew repeatedly appeared as an omen; the court ministers all composed "Sweet Dew Eulogies," and the Masters of Writing ordered Shao to write the preface.
idiomatic: Gao Yang visited Jinyang; along the way sweet dew appeared again and again; court ministers all wrote Sweet Dew Eulogies, and the masters of writing had Shao compose the preface.

literal: When Emperor Wenxuan died, in the dire rites he was much consulted; he was ordered to draft the lamentation.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan died, he was much consulted on funeral rites and ordered to draft the lamentation.

literal: Later he was given Special Advance and died.
idiomatic: Later he was granted special advance and died.

literal: Shao followed his nature in plain simplicity; inward conduct was careful and reverent; among brothers and affinal kin he was called harmonious.
idiomatic: Shao was plain by nature, careful in private conduct, and among brothers and in-laws was praised for harmony.

literal: He broadly read the classics and histories and was versed in all; in later years he especially took to the chapter-and-sentence meaning of the Five Classics and exhausted their essentials.
idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories without exception; in later years he especially pursued the Five Classics in chapter and comment, plumbing their core.

literal: For auspicious and inauspicious ritual, public and private, he was consulted; doubts were resolved and confusion removed—he was the age's compass.
idiomatic: On ritual, public or private, he was consulted; he cleared doubt and served as the age's guide.

literal: Whenever the high ministers met in council on matters touching precedent, Shao took brush and finished at once, citations ample and fitting.
idiomatic: Whenever ministers debated precedent, Shao wrote at once, citations full and apt.

literal: Edicts and court regulations from the emperor he dared fix in a moment.
idiomatic: Imperial edicts and court regulations he could settle in moments.

literal: His phrasing was grand and far-reaching, standing alone in his time.
idiomatic: His diction was vast and far-reaching, unmatched in his day.

literal: With Wen Zisheng of Jiyin he was crown of literary men; the age called them Wen and Xing.
idiomatic: With Wen Zisheng of Jiyin he stood at the head of men of letters; contemporaries called them Wen and Xing.

literal: Wei Shou of Julu, though his heaven-given talent blazed forth, was younger in years than the two; only after Zisheng's death was Xing and Wei spoken of.
idiomatic: Wei Shou of Julu, though brilliant by nature, was junior to both; only after Zisheng died were Xing and Wei named together.

literal: Though rank and substance were both weighty, he did not use talent and office to look down on others.
idiomatic: Though heavy in repute and office, he did not condescend with talent or rank.

literal: Careless and easy, he did not cultivate imposing manner; carriage, dress, and implements were only enough to serve.
idiomatic: He was informal and easy, cared nothing for pomp; carriage, dress, and gear sufficed and no more.

literal: When fasting he did not occupy the main rooms; sitting or lying he was always in one small chamber.
idiomatic: While fasting he avoided the main rooms; sitting or lying, he kept to one small chamber.

literal: Fruit and the like he sometimes set on the rafters; when guests came he lowered them and they ate together.
idiomatic: Fruit he sometimes stored on the rafters; when guests arrived he lowered it and shared it.

literal: Heaven's gift was plain substance; he was especially at ease with difference and sameness; gentlemen whether worthy or foolish he could all receive; facing guests he sometimes undid his robe to hunt lice, yet still held fierce talk.
idiomatic: His nature was plain; he was at ease with all sorts; worthy or dull, every gentleman met his courtesy; with guests he might open his robe to pick lice and still talk fiercely.

literal: He had very many books but did not much collate them.
idiomatic: He owned many books but seldom collated them.

literal: Seeing others collate books, he often laughed and said: "How very foolish—books under Heaven cannot all be read to the end; how could one again collate these?
idiomatic: Seeing others collate books, he would laugh and say, "How foolish—no one can read every book under Heaven to the end; why collate these again?

literal: Moreover, to think on a mistaken book is again a kind of pleasure.
idiomatic: Besides, to ponder a mistaken book is its own pleasure.

literal: " His wife's younger brother Li Jijie, a man of talent and learning, said to Zicai: "Most men in the world are not clever—how could thinking on mistaken books obtain anything?
idiomatic: " His wife's brother Li Jijie, a scholar, said to Zicai, "Most people are not clever—how can pondering mistaken books gain anything?

literal: " Zicai said: "If by thinking one cannot obtain it, then there is no need to labor at reading books.
idiomatic: " Zicai said, "If thought cannot obtain it, then there is no need to trouble over books at all.

literal: " With his wife he was very distant and never spent a night within.
idiomatic: " He was distant from his wife and never slept inside with her.

literal: He himself said he once entered the inner apartments by day and was barked at by a dog; having spoken he at once clapped his hands and laughed greatly.
idiomatic: He said he once entered the inner quarters by day and was barked at by a dog; saying this, he clapped his hands and laughed.

literal: His nature loved talk and appreciation and could not be idle alone; when public business ended and he rested, he always needed guests for company.
idiomatic: He loved conversation and could not sit alone; when office ended and he was at leisure, he always wanted guests beside him.
